purpose: Precondition evidence for an irreversible action: deleting the two sponsor-funded GCP compute instances. Re-measured fresh rather than reusing the earlier sweep's conclusion.
authorized_by: author, 2026-09-24: "空闲先清掉，然后在需要时在使用保证我们的数据安全即可" (clear the idle ones first, keep our data safe)
liveness_verdict: Both hosts idle: load 0.00 on all three averages, zero logged-in users, zero screens, every container Exited(0), no python/ray/grid process. Nothing was mid-write, so no partial artifact could be lost.
classification_method: Whole-home content-hash manifest per host (excluding .git internals, ~/.cache, conda pkgs, venvs, and shell dotfiles on both sides symmetrically), compared against a local index built from the repo tree AND the workspace-root scratch tree, by sha256 first and by path second.

python_bytecode.verdict: regenerable from tracked sources; not data

dpc4_traces.verdict: public DPC-4/SPEC17 trace files, identical hash on both hosts, re-downloadable; not authored by us

watch_grid_sh.verdict: authored on the VM, no local counterpart -> RESCUED

home_workspace_snapshot.verdict: an exact extraction of local git commit b85b38c ('docs: backfill commit hashes in the export and re-verification records'), which is in local history; fully reproducible with `git archive b85b38c`
home_workspace_snapshot.proof: git archive b85b38c materialised locally and hash-compared file by file: 66/66 byte-identical, 0 differing, 0 absent

trace_hash_corroboration.claim: the three trace sha256 values recorded in results/grid_fact_prompt/provenance.json were re-hashed on the live host during this sweep and matched exactly
trace_hash_corroboration.coverage_caveat: 3 of the 6 grid provenance.json files pin trace sha256 (grid_fact_prompt, grid_v6, grid_v7_gcp); the other 3 record trace names without hashes and grid_x_aggressive_s3 has no provenance.json at all. Across the three that do pin, all three traces agree on one hash each, and those hashes are the ones re-verified on the live host. So the corroboration covers half the grids that kept a provenance record, not the whole measurement set.
trace_hash_corroboration.coverage_caveat_original: only 1 of the 6 grid provenance.json files pins trace sha256 at all; the other 5 record trace names without hashes. This corroboration therefore covers one grid, not the measurement set.
trace_hash_corroboration.coverage_correction: This caveat originally read 'only 1 of the 6 grid provenance.json files pins trace sha256 at all'. That was wrong: the real number is 3. It was wrong in the direction nobody complains about, since it understated our own coverage rather than overstating it. Caught when scripts/verify_paper_claims.py tried to re-derive the '1' from the files and got 3. The original wording is kept above rather than deleted.

earlier_rescue.note: the two packed archives among them (grid_both_axes.tgz, grid_nullity_control.tgz) were unpacked and compared to the committed results/: 10/10 files byte-identical, the only local-only file being provenance.json, which is authored locally after transfer and was never on a VM

sweep_artifacts.note: raw sweep stdout kept in untracked .tmp/; this file records its hash

conclusion: No unique measurement, result, config, log or authored script remains only on either VM. The single unique authored file (watch_grid.sh) was rescued and hash-verified before deletion. Teardown is safe.
